rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references` (the `skills` query). The requirement permits a skill to put specialized material in linked files. It requires each such link to say when to read the file.

I found two references to such files, and each one says when to read it:
- **`references/review-prompt.md`** is in Workflow step 3 (Review). The step says a read-only subagent is told to read it, along with the habeas skill's `SKILL.md`, when reviewing a group of requirements. If subagents can't be started, the agent reviews each group itself "against the prompt". So the trigger is clear: it is read during the step 3 review.
- **`references/fixme.md`** is in the "Choosing references" section. It belongs to the habeas-evidence skill, not this one. The text says to use it "To defer a requirement gap the user agrees to", with `{fixme}`. That states when to read it.

The skill has no other links to files, and no link lacks a stated trigger. Neither is a markdown hyperlink. They are inline-code path references. Under the stricter reading that only markdown links count, there is nothing to violate. Under the looser reading that these references count as links, both meet the obligation. So the two readings do not lead to different conclusions.

No violation queries were listed for this site. The site meets its obligation.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
